input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), security/service-failure (9.3) and Order-Form-scope (9.5) termination rights; Sections 6.2, 19.4, 20.5 and 27.3 are likewise all cause- or event-based. No termination-for-convenience right exists for either Party, and Section 8.1 fixes a three-year term with Order Forms auto-renewing on 180 days' notice under 8.2. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule, so this fails the fallback as a missing behaviour. Favourably, Vendor also has no convenience right, so our redline adds only a Customer-side 30-day right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (supported by the existing refund mechanic in 10.2) and confirms Vendor has none.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination fee, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since Section 9 currently allows exit only for cause across a three-year term. If helpful, we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day termination-for-convenience right with pro-rata refund and confirming Vendor has no convenience right.
